name: Charles Eliakim Tupper
text:
Charles Eliakim Tupper (gen 1)
Born: 19 Aug 1748 (Plymouth, MA)
Died: 29 Apr 1822 (Cornwallis Square, Kings Co.)
Grave: Morristown Cemetery (Old), Morristown, Kings Co. NS
Parents: Eliakim Tupper Jr., Mary Bassett
Spouse: Elizabeth West
Children: Thomas Tupper
Confidence: confirmed
Notes: Sir Charles Tupper (1821 to 1915), Premier of Nova Scotia and Prime Minister of Canada, was his grandson through Rev. Charles Tupper (1794 to 1881). Conflict: one secondary source says Charles and his wife died after 1837; FamilySearch and WikiTree give 29 Apr 1821. Death year: Find a Grave gives 1822; earlier sources gave 1821.
- Came to Cornwallis Township as a boy with his Planter family about 1760 [source: A Family Reunion: Tupper (douglasjgraham.net)]
- Farmer in Cornwallis Township, according to his son's biography [source: Dictionary of Canadian Biography: Rev. Charles Tupper (1794-1881)]
- Married Elizabeth West in Cornwallis in 1771; FamilySearch lists at least 15 children [source: FamilySearch: Charles Eliakim Tupper (1748-1821)]
- Father of Rev. Charles Tupper DD (1794 to 1881), a leading Baptist minister, and grandfather of Sir Charles Tupper, Premier of Nova Scotia and Prime Minister of Canada [source: Dictionary of Canadian Biography: Rev. Charles Tupper (1794-1881)]
- Buried at Morristown Cemetery (Old), according to FamilySearch [source: FamilySearch: Charles Eliakim Tupper (1748-1821)]
Sources: WikiTree: Arthur Tupper (ancestors of Thomas H. Tupper); FamilySearch: Charles Eliakim Tupper (1748-1821); Dictionary of Canadian Biography: Rev. Charles Tupper (1794-1881)

name: Neil Carman Tupper
text:
Neil Carman Tupper (gen 7)
Born: 10 Feb 1933 (Morristown)
Died: 20 Jun 2022 (Kentville)
Grave: Morristown Cemetery, Morristown, Kings Co. NS (interment per obituary) (also on Find a Grave)
Parents: Durwood Belmont Tupper, Helen Gertrude (Haines) Tupper
Spouse: Joy Eldora (Salsman) Walsh, Mother of Neil's other 6 children (name not known)
Children: Cheryl Judy (Tupper) Hiltz, David John Tupper, Sonja Dale (Tupper) Stewart, Troy Neil Tupper, Tamara Tupper, Billiejo (Tupper) Keddy, Crystal (Tupper) Allen, Heidi Tupper, Virginia Fynes, Neil Shannon Tupper
Confidence: confirmed
- Founded and ran Fox Mountain Camping Park, Morristown [source: Neil C. Tupper obituary (Middleton FH)]
- Farmer and businessman: hogs, beef, crops, apples, Christmas trees and firewood; also a carpenter who cut and milled logs [source: Neil C. Tupper obituary (Middleton FH)]
- Member of the Hog Producers of Nova Scotia, the Christmas Tree Farmers Association, the Cat and Coonhound Club, and the Aylesford Fire Commission [source: Neil C. Tupper obituary (Middleton FH)]
- Father of 10 children [source: Neil C. Tupper obituary (Middleton FH)]
- Founded Fox Mountain Camping Park, 6128 Aylesford Road, Aylesford, in 1994 after running a hog farm and Christmas tree operation; started the Fox Mountain Bluegrass Festival and ran it for 20 years (park's own history, confirmed in substance by his obituary). [source: Trailer Parks Canada, Fox Mountain Camping Park listing]
Obituary: Morristown farmer and businessman known for hogs, beef, apples, Christmas trees and firewood, and founder of Fox Mountain Camping Park. He was a lifelong hunter and woodsman, and said his 10 children were his proudest accomplishment. His funeral was held at Morristown Baptist Church.
Sources: Neil C. Tupper obituary (Middleton FH); Salsman register (genealogy-paulsen.org); Find a Grave: Neil Carman Tupper

name: John (Jack) Elwood Murphy
text:
John (Jack) Elwood Murphy (gen 7)
Born: c. 1920 (South Berwick)
Died: 16 Aug 1995 (Valley Regional Hospital, Kentville)
Grave: Berwick Cemetery (private family burial, per obituary). Berwick Cemetery is on Main Street, Berwick, near Morse Lane (johncardinal.com/kings/cem.htm).
Parents: James Evander Murphy, Jennie May (Kirk) Murphy
Confidence: confirmed
Notes: Wife: Marjorie (Marj) Kelley. Daughters: Sharon (Bob) Trefry and Jacqueline (Gary) Roop. Grandchildren: Kellie and Kevin Trefry, Jennifer and Jonathan Roop. He had two infant sons who died before him.
- WWII: served overseas 1941 to 1945 as a gunner with an anti-aircraft battery; wounded in action [source: John (Jack) Elwood Murphy obituary 1995 (genealogybuff)]
- Life member and past president of Royal Canadian Legion Branch 69 in Berwick; served with the Canadian Corps of Commissionaires [source: John (Jack) Elwood Murphy obituary 1995 (genealogybuff)]
- Owned and ran a garage and restaurant in South Berwick; retired as a foreman with the Department of Highways [source: John (Jack) Elwood Murphy obituary 1995 (genealogybuff)]
- Played baseball with the Berwick Apple Kings and coached women's softball [source: John (Jack) Elwood Murphy obituary 1995 (genealogybuff)]
Obituary: Served overseas from 1941 to 1945 as a gunner in WWII and was wounded in action. He was a life member and past president of Royal Canadian Legion Branch 69 in Berwick. He ran a garage and restaurant in South Berwick and retired as a foreman with the Department of Highways.
Sources: John (Jack) Elwood Murphy obituary 1995 (genealogybuff transcription); Find a Grave: John (Jack) Elwood Murphy

name: Emery Albert (Alfred) Salsman
text:

Born: 9 Oct 1881 (New Ross, Lunenburg Co.)
Died: 20 Sep 1965 (Berwick)

Parents: David Henry (Daniel) Saltzman, Sarah Priscilla (Legge) Saltzman
Spouse: Addie S. (Rogers) Salsman
Children: Noble Richard Salsman
Confidence: confirmed
Notes: He was a cooper and farmer at Cornwallis and later Waterville. He married Addie in Kentville on 9 Nov 1903 and they had 11 children. Earlier generations in the register: David Henry (Daniel) Saltzman, then Henry Jollymore, George Michael Salzmann, Casper Friedrich, and Isac. Conflicts: his middle name is 'Albert' on Find a Grave and 'Alfred' in the registers. His birthplace is New Ross on Find a Grave and Norwood Settlement in the registers (both in Lunenburg Co.).
- Cooper and farmer at Cornwallis (1911 census) and Waterville (1921 census), where the family owned its home [source: Salsman register: Emery Alfred Salsman family]
- Cooper at Cornwallis in 1911; farmer at Waterville in 1921, when sons Noble and Roy were coopers making barrels (census, via Saltzman Register). [source: Saltzman Register (genealogy-paulsen.org), Sixth Generation, #325]
